metaDescription: Six bed and nightstand phone stands compared by arm length, clamp range and stability, for hands-free video, audiobooks and calls while lying down.
introParagraphs: Holding a phone above your face in bed tires your arms and drops it on your nose. A bed phone stand either clamps to a headboard or bed frame on a bendable gooseneck arm, or sits on the nightstand as a tabletop stand. This guide compares six: the Lamicall 38-inch gooseneck, the Lamicall 33.4-inch gooseneck, the SAIJI gooseneck, the Selfdee gooseneck, the tounee tabletop stand and the POQOD foldable stand.

The gooseneck group is where the numbers matter. The Lamicall's overall length is 38 inches with a 35 inch arm, the SAIJI arm is 33.46 inches (85 centimeters) and made of 8.5 mm aluminum alloy, the other Lamicall is 33.4 inches with a clamp opening of 0 to 2.36 inches, and the Selfdee clamps surfaces up to 1.5 inches thick. The tounee and POQOD are not clamps, so they suit nightstands rather than headboards.

We evaluated each on product specs and buyer feedback, not claimed hands-on lab work. We weighed arm reach, clamp compatibility with your bed, how well the arm holds position and the phone sizes supported.

products.name: Lamicall 38-Inch Nylon Braided Gooseneck Holder

specList.label: Arm
specList.value: Nylon braided with aluminum alloy core

products.description:
The Lamicall 38-inch is the longest-reaching holder in this guide, with a 35 inch arm in a 38 inch overall length. The nylon braided wrap and aluminum alloy core let it bend and hold. A 360-degree ball joint and rotating clamp let you set the screen above your face or beside your pillow.

The long arm is the main advantage for lying on your side or back, because it carries the phone to a comfortable viewing distance. It suits phones from 4 to 7 inches, covering almost all smartphones. The tradeoff is that a longer arm can sway more than a shorter one, and it sits in the highest price tier.

It clamps to a bed frame or headboard. Compared with the 33.4-inch Lamicall, it adds reach. Compared with the SAIJI, it uses a braided wrap instead of a telescopic arm.
products.bestFor: Lying on your back or side with the screen above you
pros: 38 inch overall length with a 35 inch arm
Aluminum alloy core holds its shape
cons: Highest price tier of the group

products.name: Lamicall 33.4-Inch Gooseneck Bed Phone Holder
products.description:
The 33.4-inch Lamicall is the value pick, reworked after complaints about shaky holders that sag over time. Its adjustable clamp base opens from 0 to 2.36 inches, so it grips many headboards and frames. The full adjustable arm keeps a stable position.

It is built for watching streaming hands-free in bed or on the sofa and for FaceTime calls. It installs quickly with a screw clamp. The tradeoff is that it is shorter than the 38-inch version, and the 2.36 inch clamp limit can exclude thick headboards.

It sits in a mid-range tier. Compared with the SAIJI, it offers a clearer clamp spec. Compared with the Selfdee, it opens narrower.
products.bestFor: A reliable headboard clamp for streaming and calls
cons: Clamp too narrow for thick headboards

products.name: SAIJI Gooseneck Bed Phone Holder
products.description:
The SAIJI has a 33.46 inch (85 centimeter) telescopic arm that rotates 360 degrees. The arm is made of 8.5 mm aluminum alloy, which the maker says resists fracture. The holder fits phones with screens from 4.0 to 6.3 inches.

The telescopic arm lets you adjust the distance to your eyes. The thick alloy arm is reassuring if you worry about bending fatigue. The tradeoff is that larger phones above 6.3 inches fall outside its range, and the listing is less detailed about clamp opening.

It sits in a mid-range tier. Compared with the Lamicall 33.4-inch, it offers a thicker arm but a vaguer clamp spec. Compared with the Selfdee, it is more fully specified.
products.bestFor: Adjusting distance to your eyes with a thick arm
cons: Phones above 6.3 inches do not fit

products.name: Selfdee Gooseneck Bed Phone Holder
products.description:
The Selfdee is a flexible gooseneck that clamps onto any surface up to 1.5 inches thick. The hard metal stand and 360-degree rotating arm let you mount it on a bed, desk, chair or table. It is a universal mount for the bedroom and beyond.

The clamp is versatile, so you can move it from the bed to the kitchen. The tradeoff is that the listing offers fewer exact specs than the Lamicall or SAIJI, and the 1.5 inch limit is tighter than some headboards. It sits in a low-cost tier.

It is a simple all-purpose holder. Compared with the SAIJI, it offers less detail. Compared with the 38-inch Lamicall, it is shorter and cheaper.
products.bestFor: Moving one holder between bed, desk and kitchen
cons: 1.5 inch clamp limit may be tight

products.name: tounee 8 to 11 Inch Adjustable Phone Stand

specList.label: Case
specList.value: Width up to 9.5 cm, thickness up to 1.5 cm

products.description:
The tounee is not a clamp but a tabletop stand that suits a nightstand. It extends from 8 to 11 inches with 50 degrees of tilt, and a weighted metal base with non-slip silicone pads keeps it steady. It fits phones with cases up to 9.5 centimeters wide and 1.5 centimeters thick.

On a bedside table it raises the phone toward your face while you lie propped on pillows. It will not hang over the bed like a gooseneck, so it works best when you sit up. The tradeoff is that the angle does not reach a phone held above a flat-lying face.

It sits in a mid-range tier. Compared with the POQOD, it is far steadier. Compared with the Lamicall, it needs a tabletop.
cons: Does not hang over the bed

products.name: POQOD Foldable Phone Stand 2-Pack
products.description:
The POQOD is a featherweight foldable stand sold as a pair. It supports 4 to 10 inch phones, tablets and e-readers with five angle slots. At about half an ounce, it folds flat.

As a nightstand stand it is simple: place it, set a slot and watch. The tradeoff is that it is very light, so it can slide or tip on a soft surface. It cannot clamp or hang over the bed.

It sits in the lowest price tier. Compared with the tounee, it is lighter but less stable. Compared with the gooseneck holders, it only works on a flat surface.
products.bestFor: A cheap spare for a flat nightstand

buyingCriteria.explanation: Bed holders range from about 60 cm to 38 inches, and reach decides whether the phone hangs over your face. The Lamicall 38-inch has a 35 inch arm, the SAIJI 33.46 inches and the other Lamicall 33.4 inches. Longer arms reach more but sway more. Match reach to how you lie.

Check that your headboard or frame fits the clamp. The Lamicall 33.4-inch opens 0 to 2.36 inches and the Selfdee grips up to 1.5 inches. Measure your headboard first, since thick wood may not fit. A bad fit is the top reason for returns.

Goosenecks can sag with use, which is why the Lamicall 33.4-inch was reworked. The SAIJI uses an 8.5 mm aluminum alloy arm, and the 38-inch Lamicall has an aluminum alloy core. A stiffer arm holds position longer. Keep the phone's weight modest.

Check the device width range and weight limit including the case. The Lamicall 38-inch handles 4 to 7 inch phones, the SAIJI 4.0 to 6.3 inches, and the tounee fits cases up to 9.5 cm wide. Universal fit is marketing. Verify your phone.

Bed options include gooseneck mounts or headboard clamps, and the headboard must fit the clamp. Tabletop stands like the tounee and POQOD suit nightstands but cannot hang over you. Decide whether you lie flat or sit propped up. Flat lying favors a gooseneck.
A heavier base with non-slip padding resists tipping, as on the tounee. For limited dexterity, favor few adjustment steps. A gooseneck bends with one hand. Test the grip before bedtime use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and mounting
howWeEvaluated.description: The Lamicall 38-inch with a 35 inch arm scored highest, while tabletop stands scored lower for lying down. We judged from specs and buyer feedback, not lab trials.

howWeEvaluated.title: Clamp compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored stated clamp openings. The Lamicall 33.4-inch at 0 to 2.36 inches and the Selfdee at 1.5 inches scored well, while the SAIJI lost points for vagueness. A clear spec helps you check your bed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Arm strength
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered materials. The SAIJI's 8.5 mm alloy and the Lamicall's aluminum core scored best. Reworked sag resistance earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Phone size support
howWeEvaluated.description: The tounee and POQOD handle larger devices, while the SAIJI caps at 6.3 inches. The strongest pick, the Lamicall 38-inch, outranks the most basic, the POQOD, for bed use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the price tier
howWeEvaluated.description: The POQOD is lowest-cost, the Selfdee is low-cost, and the Lamicall 38-inch is highest. We credit clamps that fit.

cards.label: Gooseneck clamp
cards.text: The Lamicall models, SAIJI and Selfdee hang the phone over you. They need a headboard or frame that fits.

cards.label: Nightstand stand
cards.text: The tounee and POQOD sit on a table and suit propped-up viewing. Recommendation: gooseneck if you lie flat, tabletop if you sit up.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A long arm that holds position, a clamp that fits and a phone range that covers your device. Avoid sagging arms.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Lamicall 38-Inch has the longest arm, and the 33.4-Inch is the value alternative. Choose the 38-Inch for reach and the 33.4-Inch for value.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use it nightly lying down, where the Lamicall 38-Inch reach and core pay off.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use it occasionally, where the Selfdee or POQOD at lower tiers are enough.

faq.q: How do I choose between a gooseneck and a tabletop stand?
faq.a: A gooseneck like the Lamicall hangs the phone over you for lying flat. A tabletop stand like the tounee suits propped-up viewing. Choose by your position.
Bed holders range from lowest-cost to highest tier. The Lamicall 33.4-inch balances value. Spend more for reach.

faq.q: How do I check my headboard fits?
faq.a: Measure its thickness and compare with the clamp opening, such as 0 to 2.36 inches on the Lamicall. Wood and metal frames differ. Measure first.
Some goosenecks sag with time, which is why the 33.4-inch Lamicall was reworked. A thick alloy arm like the SAIJI's holds longer. Keep the phone light.

faq.q: Can I use it with a large phone?
faq.a: The Lamicall 38-inch supports 4 to 7 inches and the SAIJI up to 6.3. Larger phones may need the tounee or POQOD. Check width.

faq.q: Is it safe to use in bed?
faq.a: A stable clamp keeps the phone from falling on you. Check the grip each time. Avoid overloading the arm.

faq.q: How do I clean the holder?
faq.a: Wipe the arm and clamp with a damp cloth and dry. Check the screw for tightness. Avoid solvents.
